subject: Production: sudden curtailed throughput due to rate controls
messages:
From: Amelia Reyes <amelia.reyes@healthlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Collins <peter.collins@healthlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden curtailed throughput due to rate controls

Laura —

We started seeing a sudden drop in processed requests this morning (approx 08:12 PT) for our main ingestion pipeline. Latency spiked (p95 from ~120ms to >1.2s) and a large fraction of requests are receiving 429/ResourceExhausted responses. Throughput for our tenant fell by ~60%.

We attached a small sample of request/response headers and traces (healthlytics-logs-20270801.zip). Our SREs have confirmed the issue correlates with a change in Redwood’s rate control behavior but we don’t have visibility into what policy changed. This is impacting several live customers and our monitoring is on high alert.

Can you triage urgently and tell us what changed on your side? We need an ETA and whether an emergency rollback is possible. If this is a quota/burst window change, it needs immediate attention — business impact is material.

Thanks,
Amelia Reyes
SRE Lead, HealthLytics
[Attachment: healthlytics-logs-20270801.zip (application/zip)]
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Reyes <amelia.reyes@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Peter Collins <peter.collins@healthlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden curtailed throughput due to rate controls

Amelia —

Thanks for the fast report and the logs. I’m escalating this to our on-call policy/edge team now (cc’ing Marissa). Initial read: we pushed a policy adjustment to burst-window defaults yesterday evening in the US region; Marissa will confirm whether that touched per-tenant rollout flags.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Marissa / Ops: can you confirm whether any policy that constrains per-tenant burst window or window-size landed in the last 24h and whether a targeted rollback is available?
- HealthLytics: if you have exact tenant-id(s) you can share, please reply so we can scope quickly.

I’ll keep you updated every 15–30m; if we need to escalate to execs for a one-time remediation/credit we’ll do that too. Apologies for the disruption.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: emergency-rollback-plan.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden curtailed throughput due to rate controls

Laura / Jonas —

Quick technical summary from ops triage (what we found so far):
- We shipped policy rollout PR #4823 at 01:18 UTC yesterday which updated default burst-window and per-tenant window sharding behavior for the US region.
- A validation flag that scopes the new window granularity to "region-only" failed to apply for customers with legacy tenant manifests; HealthLytics tenants were caught by an unexpected manifest shape.
- As a result, their effective "burst window" dropped from the expected 5m to ~10s for a subset of routes, which explains the sudden 429s and the sharp reduction in throughput.

Immediate recommendation:
1) Emergency rollback of PR #4823 for the US region (manual revert + redeploy) — estimated time to rollback and redeploy: 25–40 minutes depending on canary progress.
2) Temporary customer-scoped override: add HealthLytics tenant-IDs to the backward-compatible window map to restore the 5m behavior while we stabilize the rollout.
3) Post-incident: add manifest-shape validation to the rollout gating and a one-time compatibility check for customers flagged as "legacy."

I’ve attached a compact diff showing the policy delta (policy-diff.txt). If we have approval to proceed with rollback I’ll coordinate the redeploy and provide minute-by-minute updates.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Production Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: policy-diff.txt (text/plain)]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Reyes <amelia.reyes@healthlytics.com>, Peter Collins <peter.collins@healthlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden curtailed throughput due to rate controls — exec brief and ask

Team / HealthLytics leadership —

Summary (for execs):
- Impact: HealthLytics observed a ~60% drop in throughput and elevated p95 latency; customer reports began at ~08:12 PT on 2027-08-01.
- Root cause: policy rollout PR #4823 changed burst-window defaults and unintentionally reduced per-tenant window length for customers with legacy tenant manifests.
- Scope: affected a small cohort of tenants in US region; initial estimate 12 active tenants, HealthLytics among the most impacted.

Actions taken:
- 2027-08-01 10:30 PT: performed targeted override for HealthLytics tenant-IDs; throughput recovered to baseline within ~8 minutes for verified routes.
- 2027-08-02 09:10 PT: completed emergency rollback of PR #4823 in US region; rolling canaries show stable behavior.
- We have queued a postmortem and compatibility validation task to prevent recurrence.

Exec asks:
1) Approve a one-time customer credit for HealthLytics to cover the impacted window (proposal: 25% usage credit for the 6-hour incident window).
2) Approve an ops playbook change: require manifest-shape gating for any rollout touching per-tenant policy logic.

HealthLytics — apologies again for the impact. Marissa/Neha will follow with the postmortem and a proposed communication to your stakeholders. Laura — please confirm whether the credit proposal is acceptable and if you want me to draft the external note.

Jonas Weber
VP, Service Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Related link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy/commit/abc123def]
